what: UI-side numbers for map/globe.js: palettes, camera, haze, shading, label styles; every value traces to ui/basemap/*.json

globe_palette.source: ui/basemap/palette-globe.json (pipeline/basemap/globefit.py on the Maps App globe screenshot)

haze.status: not drawn any more (RENDER-PIPELINE 6: the inner darkening is the n.L term + rim; kept as verification data)

shading.status: replaced by the shader formula in map/globe-light.js (SHADER-NUMBERS 4.1); kept as the verification fit

city.halo_note: taken from the capital (Tokyo) measurement; Busan's own halo read land-green

graticule_line.source: native-nosidebar.png darkest dash pixels rows 930-938, x 1400-1520 (2x)

city_marker.source: native.png Tokyo marker luminance print (ring 92, core 254), 2026-09-16

ground.what: ground colour rasters for the z5-8 overlay band: Landcover sheet colour x groundSettings climate tint x flat-ground light, sRGB-encoded
ground.formula: sRGB(linearise(fillColor) tinted by (temperature, aridity) HSV cells, bilinear, x light(0,0,1))

sheet.note: Apple z = MapLibre z + 1; band containing Apple z6 = the MapLibre z5 acceptance view

hsv.cells: 3x3 per class, axes add (SHADER-NUMBERS 4.4), sampled bilinearly by the codes below

geolines.note: Apple zoom bands; dash units quarter-pt; lum adjustments are HSL lightness points (RENDER-PIPELINE 7.13)

ground_globe.what: globe ground rasters from Apple's SPR tiles (VECTOR_SPR_MERCATOR z2-3) decoded with GeoServices' GEOVectorTile; see RENDER-PIPELINE 2.4-2.5
ground_globe.class_index_255: no Apple tile in the cache copy (alpha 0 in the albedo rasters)

climate.temp_codes: 0 Arctic 1 VeryCold 2 Cold 3 Cool 4 Warm 5 Hot 6 VeryHot (VectorKit gss enum strings); cell = 1 + (T-3)/3
climate.arid_codes: 0 VeryWet 1 Wet 2 Moist 3 SemiDry 4 Dry 5 VeryDry; cell = 1 + (A-3)/3 for A<3, 1 + (A-3)/2 for A>=3 (SHADER-NUMBERS 3.2)

height.source: DaVinci terrain mesh (chapter 100) vertex z x tileSizeInMeters x cos(lat); vertex spacing ~25 km at z3, ~50 km at z2
height.note: z1-4 groundElevationScale 14 / 9 / 7 / 5 is what makes the App's z3 globe look mountainous (RENDER-PIPELINE 2.5)

dvmt_globe.source: ui/basemap/dvmt-materials.json (pipeline/basemap/dvmt.py <- DvMt tileset 60 of the geod cache); variant client:69=0 (globe), client:1 0 day / 1 night

stars.format: basemap/data/globe/stars-format.md (10000 x float32[3]: angle 0-2pi, angle +-1.54, brightness 14.08->10.02)

used_for: light direction, light/ambient colours, irradiance cube (globe-light.js)

hillshade.light: azimuth 240 deg / altitude 65 deg from shader-numbers.json lighting (RENDER-PIPELINE 7.4)
hillshade.strength: hillshadeAlpha(z) in map/globe.js: alpha = (lightColor*cos(alt)/light(0,0,1)/2.2) * groundElevationScale(z+1) / (0.625 * 2^(0.3*(15-(z+1)))) — MapLibre 'standard' method, exaggeration 0.5

pending.what: values still SAMPLED off App screenshots (used only below the PAL hand-over or where no decoded source exists)
pending.globe_palette: App-globe ocean bands / land tints (palette-globe.json): retired 2026-09-17 - the globe paints the DvMt globe materials (dvmt_globe) on Apple's rasters; kept as the verification of those colours (humid #e9f6d8 vs Forest x light #e3f1d8, 1000-2000 m #a9d6f1 vs ramp #a2ddf9); only the camera fit is still used
pending.climate_globe_png: sampled pastel Koppen tints: only the no-tile fallback under Apple's rasters (Americas, southern hemisphere)
pending.shelf: 0-200 m shelf raster (palette-shelf.json): retired 2026-09-17, the DvMt water ramp covers 0-7 km
pending.labels_app / labels: label typography measured on App renders; the globe sheet rows (globe-key-numbers.tsv) are decoded but not yet wired to the DOM labels
pending.background.stars: star size 1.2 pt and grey levels: GlobeStars vertex point-size/alpha formula not decoded; positions/brightness order now from stars.bin

background.limb_source: native.png row 800 (2x), Maps App globe screenshot
